ch36.d.slits: Number of slits: one (single-slit diffraction) or two of the same width $a$ (double slit = interference × diffraction)
ch36.d.d: Distance $d$ between the centres of the two slits
ch36.d.lambda: Wavelength $\lambda$ of the incoming light, shown as its colour
ch36.d.D: Distance $D$ from the slit to the screen
ch36.d.yp: Screen point for the paths (one slit: the source pair; two slits: the two slit centres); drag the white dot on the screen
ch36.s.goal.cause: Cause of diffraction: every point in the slit acts as a new source (Huygens sources), and their waves interfere
ch36.s.goal.min: First minimum: each source in the upper half pairs with one half a slit below; every pair differs in path by $\lambda/2$ and cancels, so $a\sin\theta = \lambda$
ch36.s.goal.two: Two slits: the two-slit interference fringes ($\cos^2\beta$) sit inside the single-slit diffraction envelope ($(\sin\alpha/\alpha)^2$); a bright fringe that falls on an envelope minimum is missing
ch36.s.obs.build: Play: the wave spreads out behind the slit and the screen builds up a wide central maximum and weak outer maxima
ch36.s.obs.pair: Default point (first minimum): the top source (blue) and the source half a slit below it (orange) differ in path by $\Delta L \approx 0.5\lambda$, and so does every other pair
ch36.s.obs.narrow: Slit width 1 μm: the central maximum spreads wide ($\sin\theta_1 = \lambda/a$)
ch36.s.obs.wide: Slit width 6 μm ($a \gg \lambda$): the light goes nearly straight through, a bright band about as wide as the slit (the shadow of geometric optics)
ch36.s.obs.lambda: Wavelength 400 → 700 nm (settings): the same slit spreads the light wider
ch36.s.obs.two: Two slits (default $a$ = 2 μm, $d$ = 4 μm, $d/a = 2$): three bright fringes inside the central envelope (grey dashed line); the $m = \pm2$ fringes fall on the first envelope minimum $y_1$ and are missing. At the default point $\Delta L \approx 2\lambda$ (constructive), yet it is dark
ch36.s.obs.ratio: Slit width 1.5 μm, separation 4.5 μm in settings ($d/a = 3$): five bright fringes inside the central envelope ($2d/a - 1$), $m = \pm3$ missing
ch36.s.assume.model: 2D model: the slit is a row of Huygens point sources, amplitude $\propto r^{-1/2}$, no reflection from the barrier
ch36.s.assume.scale: The screen distance is scaled down to μm to fit the stage. Fraunhofer condition $a^2/(\lambda D) \ll 1$: up to 1 the first minimum lies at $y_1$ and drops below 3 % of the maximum. From 1 to 3 the minimum stays at $y_1$ but fills in (3–28 % of the maximum), so the $y_1$ mark is drawn faint. Above 3 (e.g. $a$ = 6 μm, $\lambda$ = 400 nm, $D$ = 15 μm, value 6) the minimum moves away from $y_1$ or disappears, and the brightest point can lie near $y_1$ (Fresnel diffraction), so the $y_1$ mark is hidden
ch36.s.assume.sources: The 10 dots in the slit (two slits: 5 each) are for illustration; the wave is computed with sources spaced at most $\lambda/2$ apart
ch36.s.assume.two: Two slits: for $d < a$ the slits touch and $d = a$ is used. Grey dashed line: $(\lvert E_1\rvert + \lvert E_2\rvert)^2$, the sum of the amplitudes each slit gives alone. The screen is close ($D \gg ad/\lambda$ does not hold), so a missing fringe is weak but not exactly zero
ch36.d.theta: Angle $\theta$ from the slit to the screen point; dragging the dot on the graph also changes it
ch36.d.N: Number $N$ of sources across the slit, one phasor arrow each
ch36.ph.goal.chain: Each source's wave is one phasor arrow; the phase difference of neighbouring sources is the angle between neighbouring arrows
ch36.ph.goal.min: The sum $E_\theta$ runs from the start to the end of the chain. When the chain closes into a circle the sum is 0: a minimum
ch36.ph.obs.zero: Angle 0°: all arrows in a line, the sum is the largest, $E_m$
ch36.ph.obs.min: Default (14.5°, near the first minimum): the two edges of the slit differ in phase by $\phi = 360°$ and the chain closes once around a circle
ch36.ph.obs.second: Larger angles: the chain winds more than once, leaving a small sum (an outer maximum), then closes again after two turns (second minimum, $a\sin\theta = 2\lambda$)
ch36.ph.obs.a: Narrower slit: smaller phase difference at the same angle, the chain curls less, so the central maximum is wider
ch36.ph.obs.N: Changing the number of sources (settings) leaves the minima in place: they are set by the edge-to-edge phase difference $\phi$
ch36.ph.assume.far: Screen very far away (Fraunhofer diffraction): rays from all sources are parallel
ch36.ph.assume.draw: The slit on the left is an enlarged sketch; the graph and $I/I_m$ are the sum of $N$ sources. The minima are those of $(\sin\alpha/\alpha)^2$ for a continuous slit ($N \ge 8$). The outer maxima are higher than for a continuous slit by $[(\phi/2N)/\sin(\phi/2N)]^2$: 1.1–1.2 times at the defaults ($a$ = 2 μm, $N$ = 10), 6.8 times at the 34° maximum for $a$ = 4 μm, $\lambda$ = 400 nm, $N$ = 8 (0.023 against 0.0034). All of them stay below 0.06; more sources bring the sum closer to the continuous slit
